description_en: This Gaṇeśa Mandira faces south, a characteristics trait of the Gaṇeśa temples and shrines in the Kathmandu Valley. An aniconic stone worshipped as the main deity is placed in the middle of the sanctum (garbhagṛha). Atoraṇacaps the aniconic stone. An icon of Nṛtyamagna (dancing) Gaṇeśa statue is carved on the middle of thetoraṇa.Another defining feature of the Gaṇeśa temples and shrines, especially in Patan, is the presence of a Nandī statue which is placed also in this temple in front of the main deity, inside the sanctum. Another such a unique feature is a dedicatedphalcāto sing devotional songs or hymns (bhajana) adjacent to the temples. There is aphalcāright in front of this Mandira too. The tradition of singingbhajanain thephalcāstopped nearly three decades ago (source: local knowledge, member of Gaṇeśa Guṭhī, Rājopādhyāya, male, age 52).The residents of Pātako, Mvaḥmadu Galli and Dathujhyāḥ Ṭola worship the main deity of this Mandira as their local deity (sthānaor vernacular ‘thānaGaṇeśa’). Aguṭhīcomprising of local Rājopādhyāya Brahmins is still functioning. Theguṭhīmembers place a metal Gaṇeśa statue in the sanctum during Yẽnyāḥ Punhi for special worship (pūjā) and it is also displayed for the public.No documented evidence about the initial construction is present. In NS 1021 (1901 CE) stones were paved in thegarbhagṛha. In VS 1987 (1930 CE), a golden parasol (chatra) was donated to the Mandira. The latest restoration of the temple, after the 2015 earthquake, was done by the Department of Archaeology.
description_ne: उपत्यकाका अधिकांश गणेश मन्दिरहरू झैं यो मन्दिर पनि दक्षिणतिर फर्काई बनाइएको छ ।  मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र गणेशको रूपमा पूजिने अमूर्त ढुङ्गा छ । उक्त ढुङ्गालाई बीचमा पारी तोरण चढाइएको छ ।  तोरणको मध्य भागमा नृत्यमग्न गणेश कुँदिएको छ । पाटनका प्राय गणेश मन्दिरहरूमा गणेशको सामुन्ने नन्दिको मूर्ति पाइन्छ । यस मन्दिरभित्र पनि गणेश मानिने अमूर्त ढुङ्गाको सामुन्ने नन्दिको मूर्ति स्थापित छ । गणेश मन्दिरसंगै गणेशको नाममा भजन गर्न फल्चा पनि बनेको हुनुलाई पाटनभित्रका गणेश मन्दिरहरूमा पाइने साझा विशेषता मान्न सकिन्छ । यो मन्दिरको पनि ठिक अगाडि फल्चा छ । करिब तीन दशक अघिसम्म उक्त फल्चामा भजन हुने गर्दथ्यो (Local knowledge, member of Gaṇeśa guṭhī, Rājopādhyāya, male, age 52) । पट्को, म्वःमदुगल्ली र दथुतःझ्याः टोलका निवासीले यस गणेशलाई स्थान गणेशका रूपमा पूज्दै आएका छन् । यस गणेशसंग सम्बन्धित स्थानीय ब्राह्मणहरूको अवद्धता रहेको गुठी अस्तित्वमा छ । उक्त गुठीले येँयाःपुन्हीका दिन धातुको गणेश मूर्ति गर्भगृहमा प्रदर्शनमा राखी विशेष पूजा गर्ने चलन चलाउँदै आएको आएको छ ।मन्दिरको प्रारम्भिक निर्माणमिति उल्लेखित अभिलेख मन्दिर परिसरमा पाइँदैन । नेसं १०२१ मा गर्भगृहभित्र ढुङ्गा छापिएको थियो भने विसं १९८७ मा मन्दिरमाथि सुवर्ण छत्र चढाइएको थियोे ।  मन्दिरको पछिल्लो जीर्णोद्धारकार्य सन् २०१५ को भूकम्प पश्चात् पु्रातत्व विभागबाट भएको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of a royal water channel
historical_events.event_description: A Licchavi inscription from Samvat 48 (624 CE) which is not related to this monument is in the temple premises.[1]It is not clear why this was moved to this temple. The inscription records the restoration of a water channel by Aṃśu Varman (see the edition and translation of the inscription inVajrācāryaVS 2030, 401-404).^According to Vajrācārya (VS 2030, 401), this inscription is related to Chinnamastā Mandira.

historical_events.event_name: Pavement of stone and installation of a donor statue
historical_events.event_description: The inscription records that Maṇirāja Thakālī, a resident of Dathutaḥjhyāḥ Ṭola paved stones on the temple premises and installed his and his wife’s statue there. It further informs us that he made Gaṇeśa happy by reciting the texts dedicated to him and meditating on him.
Tīrthāraja, a resident of Pasala Bāhāḥ offered a gilded banner (patāḥ) to the temple.
A marble plate only containing two names (Dhīrjamāna Sīṃ and Kājimāna Sīṃ) is posted on the northern wall inside the sanctum. It does not explain what these two people did for the temple.
The inscription records that the roof of the temple was gilded during the reign of King Thribhuvana by Kīrtimāya, Śeṣa Narasiṃ, Bekhālāla, Bhekharatna Siṃ, Anantalāla and so forth.
